sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 covers the western edge of Jersey City along the Hackensack River, drawn at 150 feet to an inch rather than the 50 feet of the street sheets. It shows the salt meadow between the river and the Morris Canal, which runs down the eastern side of the sheet beside Water Street and its tow path and turns west at the north end, below Clendenny Avenue, to a basin and lock at the river. A small pump station and a frame building stand at the lock. The meadow is divided only by long property lines running from the canal towards the river and is crossed by the river's tidal margin, drawn in blue; two dashed lines mark the state's exterior lines for piers and for solid filling along the river. Large block numbers 1746 1/2 and 1751 are printed across the meadow. The east margin carries the ends of Williams, Virginia, Ege, Clarke, Yale and Claremont Avenues where they reach Water Street, Claremont Avenue being marked closed; the blocks east of Water Street are left to sheets 3, 6 and 5. Near the south edge the Newark and New York Railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey) crosses the meadow and the canal on an embankment. No buildings stand on the meadow itself. The north edge is marked 'See Volume Five' and the south edge 'See Volume Nine'.
notes: Drawn at 150 ft to an inch.
Claremont Avenue is marked closed at Water Street.
Placed from two hand-picked points on Water Street (Clarke and Claremont Avenues), 513 ft apart; the meadow and canal are now built over by Route 440 and the Hackensack waterfront.

150 ft. Hackensack River meadow west of the Morris Canal and Water Street, Clendenny Av at top; placed from two hand-picked Water St junctions (Clarke, Claremont); low confidence; to be checked with carried points from sheets 3, 5, 6.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the northern edge of the Jersey City district west of West Side Park, in the sheet's own orientation with the long avenues running up and down the page. Marcy Avenue forms the top boundary and Mallory Avenue the bottom, with the margins above and below marked 'See Volume Five' because the continuing ground is drawn in that volume. Three long blocks, numbered 1750, 1747 and 1745, lie between Clendenny Avenue on the left, Lexington Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue in the middle, and the diagonal line of Communipaw Avenue on the right, which runs along the edge of the area marked 'See Volume Five' beside West Side Park. Almost all of the ground is divided into narrow, deep, empty lots with lot numbers printed along the frontages, so the sheet is largely open land at this date. Building is confined to a scatter of small frame dwellings and outbuildings, a few stores and saloons along the Communipaw Avenue side and near Mallory Avenue, and a workshop and a junk yard on Clendenny Avenue. The middle block, 1747, holds the works of the Port Richmond Fireworks Company, manufacturers of fireworks, drawn as a ring of scattered small sheds and magazines in an open yard, with a dilapidated iron-clad building and a hydrant shown. At the left edge the ends of Morton, Everett and Miller Streets from the neighbouring sheet are labelled. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 to 70 feet are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right.
notes: Mallory Avenue is Mallory Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the street drawn along the bottom is partly named Marcy Avenue there, and the junctions at Lexington and Roosevelt along the bottom were matched to nodes with that name.
The drawn Communipaw Avenue runs diagonally; the modern node used is Communipaw Avenue at Marcy and Mallory Avenues.
Port Richmond Fireworks Co. works occupy block 1747.
50 ft. Marcy Av to Mallory Av, Clendenny to Communipaw; Port Richmond Fireworks; turned like sheet 4. Drawn Mallory jogs; its west part is named Marcy Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers ground at the edge of the Morris Canal, with the canal curving down the left side of the page and 'See Volume Five' lettered across the top margin. Clendenny Avenue bounds the drawn area at the top, with the short stub of Marcy Avenue entering from the margin, and Williams, Boyd and Virginia Avenues cross the sheet from the canal towards the right edge. Bennett, a diagonal street marked 'not opened', runs between the blocks along the canal side, and Morton is lettered at the right edge. The blocks are numbered 1752, 1753, 1760, 1761, 1762 and 1763 and are divided into narrow deep lots, most of them empty. Building is sparse. The one named works is the Wagner Fireworks manufactory, marked not in use, with a further magazine building and sheds of the fireworks makers Sirpico and Brothers and the International Fireworks Company along a lane running north and south in block 1753. A handful of small frame dwellings stands on the lots facing Williams and Boyd Avenues near the right edge, and a stable or sheds are scattered at the rear of lots. The wedge-shaped blocks beside the canal, including the fan of lots at the top, are drawn with long narrow lots fitted to the slanted street line. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 to 60 feet are marked. The area left blank below Virginia Avenue and on the canal side belongs to neighbouring sheets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that the streets running from the canal appear nearly horizontal.
notes: Bennett is Bennett Street in OpenStreetMap.
Morton is Morton Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bennett is marked 'not opened' on the sheet.
Wagner Fireworks Manufactory is marked not in use.
50 ft. Morris Canal side, Clendenny/Williams/Boyd/Virginia, Bennett (not opened); fireworks works; turned (rot -35).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 lies between Clendenny Avenue along the top of the drawn area and Virginia Avenue along the bottom, with Mallory Avenue running up the right side and Morton at the left edge. It is drawn turned, so that Williams Avenue and Boyd Avenue cross the middle of the page as horizontal streets. Above Williams Avenue, five short blocks, numbered 1754, 1754 and a half, 1755 and 1756, are divided by Everett and Miller; Everett appears twice, as two narrow parallel streets on either side of block 1754 and a half. Below Williams Avenue the two long blocks 1760 and 1763 stretch to the right edge. The lots are narrow and deep with lot numbers printed along the frontages. Housing is a mix of two-storey frame dwellings with an occasional flat or shop, scattered along the Williams and Boyd Avenue frontages and in short rows facing Virginia Avenue, with a stable or shed at the rear of some lots. In block 1754 a fireworks store is marked near Morton. A short street named Union is drawn at the right edge, beyond Mallory Avenue, with an alarm box on it. Large parts of blocks 1760 and 1763 and of the upper blocks have no buildings. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 30 to 80 feet are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The areas outside the frame above and below carry the numbers of neighbouring sheets 2, 6, 3, 9 and 10.
notes: Morton, Everett and Miller are Morton Street, Everett Street and Miller Street; Miller Street is not in OpenStreetMap.

Everett is printed twice, on either side of block 1754 and a half; only one Everett Street survives in OpenStreetMap and it was left out of the fit because the two drawn lines could not be told apart.
50 ft. Clendenny to Virginia, Mallory at right; turned (rot -35); Everett left out (drawn twice).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 is dominated by the Crucible Steel Company of America, manufacturers of steel bars and steel wire, whose mills fill most of the page. The works lie between the Morris Canal along the top, Yale Avenue on the right, Claremont Avenue and Mallory Avenue at the bottom, and a belt of railroad tracks on the left beside Pollock Avenue, with 'See Volume Nine' lettered along the left margin. Water Street, marked not opened, runs beside the canal at the top. The large pink-coloured brick mill buildings on the right hold the tempering, patenting, rolling, wire cutting, drawing, annealing and cleaning departments, numbered 11 to 16, with hose connections and hydrants marked. In the centre stand the engine and boiler house with the independent electric plant, the draw department, the storage of wire, and, towards the lower left, a hot rolling mill with a pipe shop, store room and office. The cold rolling mill and wire mill stand at the left edge. A note in the middle describes the private fire protection: two day watchmen, three night watchmen, hourly rounds, electric lights, steam pumps and fire alarm connections in the New Jersey district. Several lines of track, including the Newark and New York Railroad, cross the left part diagonally and a branch curves in from the lower right to the works. A few frame dwellings and sheds stand on the block 1773 side of Claremont Avenue near Mallory Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned to the same orientation as the sheets to its south.
notes: Water is marked 'not opened' on the sheet; Water Street survives in OpenStreetMap only between Claremont Avenue and Clarke Avenue.
Only three control points were found, so the placement is an exact fit and low confidence.
Crucible Steel Co. of America occupies block 1775.
50 ft. Crucible Steel Co. works, Water (not opened) to Mallory; exact fit through 3 points, low confidence.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows a residential district between the Morris Canal at the top and Mallory Avenue at the bottom, with Yale Avenue, Clarke Avenue, Ege Avenue and Virginia Avenue running up and down the page. Water, marked not opened, runs along the canal at the top and Bennett, also marked not opened, crosses the upper blocks on a slant. Three very long blocks, numbered 1772, 1769 and 1766, fill the page, divided into narrow deep lots, and above Bennett short fan-shaped blocks, numbered 1767 and 1768, are fitted between the slanted streets. Almost all of the ground is empty. Buildings are limited to the rows facing Mallory Avenue at the bottom, which include frame dwellings, small flats and a stable, a short row of six matching dwellings with rear sheds near the left side of block 1772, a dairy and stables with sheds in the middle of block 1772 and block 1769, and a group of dwellings on the Virginia Avenue side of block 1766. Hydrants and six-inch and eight-inch water pipes are marked in the streets, and street widths of 60 to 80 feet are noted. A compass rose with a north arrow pointing to the upper right stands at the top left, and the scale of feet is at the bottom right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The blocks left blank at the sides belong to sheets 5, 3, 4 and 8.
notes: Bennett is Bennett Street in OpenStreetMap.
Water and Bennett are marked 'not opened' on the sheet.
50 ft. Water/Bennett to Mallory, Yale to Virginia.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows an industrial and railroad district at the head of West Side Avenue, between Mallory Avenue across the top and West Side Avenue along the bottom, with Pollock Avenue, Grant Avenue, Claremont Avenue and Yale Avenue as cross streets. The Newark and New York Railroad and a West Side connecting railroad cross the middle of the sheet in a wide band of tracks running from the upper centre down to West Side Avenue. West of the tracks are the works of the Morrin Climax Boiler Company, with machine, boiler and office buildings drawn in yellow, and below them a group of small works along Pollock and Grant Avenues, including a wagon builder, an iron working shop, a woodworking mill and the plant of F. L. Smith and Company, with a concrete block manufacturing works beside the tracks. East of the tracks, Wickes Brothers' works for contractors' machinery stand at the top, with a large pink brick warehouse, machine shop and assembling shop, and Schalkenbach and Budke's iron works, an open wagon shed and a boiler shop face Claremont Avenue and Yale Avenue. A row of frame dwellings with stores runs along Yale Avenue and West Side Avenue. Private fire alarm and hydrant arrangements are noted for Wickes Brothers. The lower edge, below West Side Avenue, carries 'See Volume Nine' and the continuations of Grant and Claremont Avenues in the next volume. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Grant Avenue and Claremont Avenue are drawn on both sides of West Side Avenue with a jog; OpenStreetMap has two nodes for each and both were used.
Block 1776 holds the Wickes Brothers works.
50 ft. Wickes Bros and Morrin Climax works, railroad band, Mallory to West Side Av.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the blocks between Mallory Avenue along the top and West Side Avenue along the bottom, with Yale Avenue, Clarke Avenue, Ege Avenue and Virginia Avenue running up and down the page. Three long blocks, numbered 1771, 1770 and 1765, hold narrow deep lots lined with frame dwellings, many marked as flats, and a few stores along West Side Avenue. A pink-coloured row of identical two-storey dwellings, partly drawn as a long terrace with small yards, runs down the left side of block 1765 beside Ege Avenue. A shorter pink row stands at the top of that block, and a group of stores and a church, the West Side Avenue Methodist Episcopal Church, stands on the West Side Avenue frontage of block 1770. The lower corner of the sheet has the diagonal line of West Side Avenue, labelled 60 feet, with the blocks across it numbered 12 and 13 and Kearney Avenue, Ege Avenue and Virginia Avenue shown as stubs south of it. Hydrants and water pipes are marked in the streets, and the open middle parts of the blocks are empty lots. A compass rose and the scale of feet are drawn at the lower left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Blocks 6, 7, 9, 12 and 13 are the neighbouring sheets.

The West Side Avenue Methodist Episcopal Church is drawn in block 1770.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers three long residential blocks of the West Side section of Jersey City, running from Mallory Avenue at the top to West Side Avenue at the foot. Virginia Avenue bounds the part on the left, Boyd Avenue and Williams Avenue divide the three blocks, and Union runs down the right margin. The blocks are numbered 1764, 1759 and 1758. Most frontages carry two and two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings, many marked as flats, set on narrow lots with wide open yards through the middle of each block. A few brick-filled frame houses stand on Virginia Avenue. Stores, saloons and small shops cluster along Mallory Avenue and, more densely, along West Side Avenue, where one block holds the Tioga Club and another an open air motion picture theatre with a stage and scenery building. Water pipe sizes and street widths of 60 feet are marked in every street, with fire hydrants at the corners. Boyd Avenue is drawn jogging at West Side Avenue, so the street on the far side lies to the right of the one drawn here. Neighbouring sheets 8, 10, 13 and 14 are named in the margins and in the outlines beyond West Side Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Union is Union Street in OpenStreetMap.
Boyd Avenue is drawn offset at West Side Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two Boyd / West Side Avenue nodes about 26 m apart.
50 ft. Mallory to West Side Av, Union to Virginia.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 continues the West Side blocks of Jersey City eastward from sheet 9, between Mallory Avenue at the top and West Side Avenue at the bottom. Union forms the slanting left side and Roosevelt Avenue the right, with Clendenny Avenue and Lexington Avenue dividing the three blocks, numbered 1757, 1749 and 1748. The left block extends further up the sheet than the other two, reaching a Mallory Avenue frontage near the top corner, while the middle and right blocks begin lower down at a second Mallory Avenue label. Frame dwellings and flats of two to three storeys line the streets on deep lots, with the middle block largely open behind its frontages. Public School No. 33 stands on Union, shown with its heating, lighting and hose details. A range of greenhouses lies in the right block, and small stores, an insurance office and a motion picture auto garage appear near West Side Avenue. Street widths of 40 to 60 feet and water pipe sizes are marked, and the right margin reads Volume Five with the neighbouring ground left blank. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right.
notes: Union is Union Street in OpenStreetMap.

The drawn Mallory Avenue does not agree with the OpenStreetMap Mallory Avenue on this sheet (modern junctions with Clendenny, Lexington and Roosevelt fall about 50 m from the drawn ones); only the West Side Avenue junctions were used for control.
Right margin reads See Volume Five.
50 ft. Strip between Mallory and West Side Av, Union to Roosevelt; modern Mallory Av about 50 m off the drawn line (excluded); 4 points on West Side Av plus 3 seam points carried from sheet 2.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the western end of West Side Avenue in Jersey City where the Newark and New York Railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey) cuts diagonally across the grid. Grant Avenue and Claremont Avenue run down the page as parallel streets, with Orient Avenue following the edge of the railroad on the right, and Halstead crosses between Claremont and Orient. The left blocks, numbered 1780, hold frame dwellings along Grant Avenue and Claremont Avenue, with a row of brick-filled partitions and a patent stone works near the top. The industrial centre is the Novelty Candy Co, a manufacturer of candy, drawn in detail with its power plant, packing and crystallising rooms, and Cannings Coal Yards beside it. Further down Orient Avenue stand the Duche Greaves Licorice Co factory, the Weathered Co builders of green houses and the Levinson Manufacturing Co, makers of chairs. Insurance notes for the three firms fill the upper right margin. A steel bridge, a passenger station and a freight track on the railroad are lettered. The lower blocks are mostly open ground between scattered dwellings and are subdivided into long lots. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Halstead is Halstead Street in OpenStreetMap; the junction with Orient Avenue was not measured.
Claremont Avenue bends at West Side Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two Claremont Avenue / West Side Avenue nodes about 56 m apart and both were matched.
50 ft. West Side Av, Grant and Claremont Avs, Newark and New York RR (CRR of NJ) cut, Novelty Candy and Greaves licorice works.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the strip of Jersey City between West Side Avenue at the top and Hudson Boulevard at the bottom, with the Newark and New York Railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey) running diagonally down the left. Kearney Avenue and Ege Avenue run the length of the sheet, and the long block between them, numbered 1789, is filled on the Ege Avenue side by a row of frame dwellings. Industry occupies the railroad side: W. H. Lutton, manufacturer of green houses, the Jersey Sweeper Co, makers of cleaning machinery, the Whilldin Pottery Co making flower pots, and the large Chas. H. Engler lumber yard with its lumber piles, sheds and office. In the middle of the main block are the No-Mor-Dust Chemical Co, a carriage house, hay and grain store and wagon sheds. A West Side Avenue railroad station and a freight station are drawn beside the tracks. At the top, Yale Avenue, Clarke Avenue and Ege Avenue meet West Side Avenue in offset crossings, and Orient Avenue and Halstead Street appear at the left edge belonging to sheet 11. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches and street widths of 35 to 60 feet are marked. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
Kearney Avenue is Kearney Avenue in OpenStreetMap but does not reach Hudson Boulevard there.
Printed "Halsted St."; Halstead Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. West Side Av to Hudson Blvd beside the Newark and New York RR; points nearly on one line, weak. Printed Halsted St.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 lies between West Side Avenue at the top and Hudson Boulevard at the bottom, with Ege Avenue along the left, Virginia Avenue through the middle and Boyd Avenue along the right. The two blocks are numbered 1790 and 1793. The block on the left is mostly frame dwellings on deep narrow lots, many two and a half storeys, with a few brick row houses and a plate printer, J. Clark, off Ege Avenue. The larger block holds Public School No. 24 in the upper centre, the C. F. Mueller Co factory making macaroni and egg noodles with its warehouses and coal bin on Boyd Avenue, and a garage of concrete block construction with a carpenter shop. Rows of frame dwellings line Boyd Avenue and Virginia Avenue, with an open interior used for sheds and yards. West Side Avenue stores and flats stand along the top edge. Virginia Avenue and Ege Avenue are drawn offset at West Side Avenue. Street widths of 60 feet, a 100 foot Hudson Boulevard and 6 and 8 inch water pipes are marked. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
The Boyd Avenue / West Side Avenue junction, drawn offset, was left out of the control.
50 ft. West Side Av to Hudson Blvd, Ege to Boyd.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers two blocks of the West Side section of Jersey City between West Side Avenue at the top and Hudson Boulevard at the bottom, with Boyd Avenue on the left, Union through the middle and Clendenny Avenue on the right. The blocks are numbered 1794 and 1797. Williams Avenue appears above West Side Avenue, ending at the top edge. The upper left block holds Fire Department Engine Co No 17 and the Seib Bros wood turning plant, makers of bowling balls, with a wood working shop, open and closed lumber sheds and a pile of kindling wood. St. Stephen's Episcopal Church stands in the right block with its furnace and lighting noted. Frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys fill the frontages on deep lots, with flats at several places and a row of brick buildings with stores on West Side Avenue. Brick houses mark the lower right corner. Hudson Boulevard is drawn 100 feet wide and curves at its lower right. Street widths, 6 and 12 inch water pipes and fire alarm boxes are marked. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap; Union is Union Street.
50 ft. West Side Av to Hudson Blvd, Boyd to Clendenny.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows the eastern blocks of the series between West Side Avenue at the top and Hudson Boulevard at the bottom, with Clendenny Avenue on the left, Lexington Avenue in the middle and Oxford Avenue and Clinton Avenue on the right, where the blocks narrow into a wedge. The three blocks are numbered 1798, 1801 and 1802, and Roosevelt Avenue meets West Side Avenue at the top. Frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys dominate the frontages, with flats and a few brick buildings, including stores, a drug store, bowling alleys and a laundry along West Side Avenue. The Lexington Avenue block holds a range of long greenhouses, shed buildings and a carpenter's shop, while Oxford Avenue is lined with dwellings on a diagonal street. The right margin reads See Volume Five. Hudson Boulevard is drawn 100 feet wide with curved block corners at the lower left. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and street widths of 50 to 60 feet are marked. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
Right margin reads See Volume Five.
50 ft. West Side Av to Hudson Blvd, Clendenny to Clinton.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows a residential and light commercial strip of the Bergen section of Jersey City, running from West Side Avenue at the top to Hudson Boulevard at the bottom. Four long blocks lie between Clinton Avenue on the left, Communipaw Avenue, Harrison Avenue and Bently Avenue on the right, numbered 1806, 1807 and 1811. The block between Clinton and Communipaw is built up with rows of two-storey frame dwellings, flats and a few stores, with brick stores along the West Side Avenue frontage at the upper left. A short lane runs into this block from Communipaw Avenue, and a veterinary hospital for horses and dogs stands at its lower end. The block between Communipaw and Harrison Avenues holds frame dwellings along both streets, with a large open rear area, and the Communipaw Motor Car Co. garage and show room, drawn in blue for concrete, stands at the Hudson Boulevard end. East of Harrison Avenue the blocks hold detached frame dwellings with outbuildings set well back on large lots, and Bently Avenue runs along the right edge with only its near side drawn. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches and street widths of 60 and 100 feet are marked in the streets. Hudson Boulevard crosses the foot of the sheet at a slant, with the block of sheet 17 below it, and West Side Avenue crosses the top beneath the margin note See Volume Five. Sheet 15 adjoins on the left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
Bently Avenue is printed with this spelling; OpenStreetMap has Bentley Avenue.
Tyson Lane and the lane off Communipaw Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. West Side Av to Hudson Blvd, Clinton to Bently Av.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 continues the Bergen section of Jersey City south of sheet 16, between Bentley Avenue at the top and Clinton Avenue at the bottom, from Hudson Boulevard on the left to Bergen Avenue on the right. The sheet is turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Four tiers of blocks cross it. The top tier, between Bentley Avenue and Harrison Avenue, is divided by Welsh Lane (block 1810) and holds frame dwellings and a group of brick and frame row houses along Welsh Lane, with a large pink-coloured brick dwelling near the right edge. The tier between Harrison and Communipaw Avenues (block 1808) is lined with detached frame dwellings on Harrison Avenue and a row of stores and flats along Communipaw Avenue, among them a hall marked Hudson Grange. The tier between Communipaw Avenue and Tyson Lane (block 1805) has dwellings, a narrow blue-coloured concrete building near the middle and a trade building at the right. The last tier, between Tyson Lane and Clinton Avenue (block 1804), is filled with frame dwellings and outbuildings. The streets converge towards Bergen Avenue, which crosses the right side at an angle, with water pipes and 60-foot and 100-foot street widths marked. Hudson Boulevard runs down the left side with only its near side drawn. The blocks of sheets 16, 18 and 30 are outlined without detail around the edges, and the margin carries the note See Volume Five. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
Welsh Lane and Tyson Lane are not in OpenStreetMap.
North is towards the upper left; the part fits at about -39 degrees against 58 degrees on sheet 16.
50 ft. Bentley Av to Clinton Av, Hudson Blvd to Bergen Av; turned.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows four tiers of blocks of the Bergen section of Jersey City between Clinton Avenue at the top and Union at the bottom, with Hudson Boulevard down the left side and Bergen Avenue, which slants across the right side, closing the blocks. Oxford Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Clendenny Avenue divide the tiers. The top tier (block 1803), between Clinton and Oxford Avenues, holds detached frame dwellings, with a row of pink-coloured brick dwellings against Bergen Avenue. The tier below (block 1800), between Oxford and Lexington Avenues, has dwellings scattered in deep lots, with a group of frame houses fronting Bergen Avenue at the right. Block 1799, between Lexington and Clendenny Avenues, is lined with dwellings on both frontages and carries a small lumber yard and a shed near Bergen Avenue. The bottom tier (block 1796), between Clendenny Avenue and Union, has frame dwellings on narrow lots and the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Our Savior near Bergen Avenue. Bramhall Avenue and Atlantic Avenue enter Bergen Avenue from the right as short stubs; the blocks beyond them belong to sheets 29 and 24. Sheets 15 and 14 adjoin on the left, sheet 17 above and sheet 19 below, each outlined without detail. Water pipes of 6 to 20 inches and street widths of 50, 60 and 100 feet are marked, Hudson Boulevard being the 100-foot street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap; Union is Union Street.
Atlantic Avenue (the stub at the right edge) is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and is not used as control.
50 ft. Clinton to Union, Hudson Blvd to Bergen Av; turned.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows three tiers of blocks of the Bergen section of Jersey City between Union at the top and Ege Avenue at the bottom, with Hudson Boulevard down the left side and Bergen Avenue on the right. Boyd Avenue and Virginia Avenue divide the tiers. The top tier (block 1795), between Union and Boyd Avenue, is lined with frame dwellings on both frontages and holds a small commission house and a hotel near the middle and a group of flats and dwellings at the right. The middle tier (block 1792), between Boyd and Virginia Avenues, is a mixture of dwellings, sheds and a few trade buildings, with the First Congregational Church, drawn in blue and pink, at the corner of Boyd Avenue and Bergen Avenue, and a row of pink-coloured brick dwellings facing Bergen Avenue. The bottom tier (block 1791), between Virginia and Ege Avenues, is filled with frame dwellings on narrow lots and a few outbuildings. Oak Street and Forrest Street are drawn as short stubs entering Bergen Avenue from the right. The blocks of sheets 18 and 20 are outlined above and below, and those of sheets 14, 13, 24 and 23 at the sides. Water pipes of 6 to 20 inches are marked in the streets, whose widths are 60 feet, and 100 feet for Hudson Boulevard. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap; Union is Union Street.
OpenStreetMap has two Bergen Avenue and Ege Avenue nodes about 40 m apart; the sheet draws one crossing.
50 ft. Union to Ege Av, Hudson Blvd to Bergen Av; turned.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows the lower end of the Bergen section of Jersey City, from Ege Avenue at the top to Grant Avenue at the bottom, with Hudson Boulevard crossing the sheet diagonally from the upper left and Bergen Avenue running down the right side. A broad cut of the Newark and New York Railroad crosses the upper part of the sheet from the lower left to the upper right, carried over Hudson Boulevard by an iron bridge, and its right-of-way separates block 1787 and the plot marked 1788 1/2 from block 1785 below. Block 1787 holds frame dwellings along Ege Avenue. Block 1785 has frame dwellings and flats on its lower frontage and the Bergen Storage Co., drawn in blue, near Bergen Avenue. Morton Place, Orient Avenue and Claremont Avenue cross Hudson Boulevard and separate blocks 1786 and 1784, 1782 and 1783, and 1780 and 1779, which are filled with frame dwellings and a few flats, with a group of pink-coloured brick dwellings and a larger brick building on the Bergen Avenue side. Short stubs of Kearney, Orient and Claremont Avenues enter Bergen Avenue from the right. The blocks of sheets 19, 12, 11, 22 and 21 are outlined around the edges, and the foot of the sheet carries the note See Volume Nine. Water pipes and street widths of 40, 60 and 100 feet are marked. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is John F. Kennedy Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
OpenStreetMap has two Bergen Avenue and Orient Avenue nodes 31 m apart, and two with Ege Avenue 40 m apart; the sheet draws one crossing of each.
Kearney Avenue at Bergen Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract. The railroad cut is not used as control.
50 ft. Ege to Grant, Newark and New York RR cut with iron bridge over Hudson Blvd; turned.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows three long blocks of the Bergen section of Jersey City between Bergen Avenue, which crosses the top at a slant, and Jackson Avenue at the bottom. Myrtle Avenue, Grant Avenue, Claremont Avenue and Orient Avenue run down the sheet and bound blocks 1986, 1985 and 1984. The block between Myrtle and Grant Avenues (block 1986) is built up with frame dwellings, some with pink-coloured brick additions, and a small blue building, with open ground along its upper end. The block between Grant and Claremont Avenues (block 1985) has rows of frame dwellings and flats on both frontages and a large open interior, and a row of pink-coloured brick stores faces Jackson Avenue at its foot. The block between Claremont and Orient Avenues (block 1984) is the most densely built, with frame dwellings on narrow lots along both sides, a garment factory and brick stores at the Jackson Avenue end and brick buildings at the corner of Orient Avenue. Claremont Avenue and Orient Avenue are also lettered on the short stubs that continue above Bergen Avenue from sheet 20. The left margin carries the note See Volume Nine, the area of Jersey City covered by another volume, and sheet 25 is outlined below Jackson Avenue and sheet 22 to the right. Water pipes and street widths of 60 feet are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive in OpenStreetMap (Martin Luther King Jr. Drive at Myrtle Avenue).
OpenStreetMap has two Bergen Avenue and Orient Avenue nodes 31 m apart; the sheet draws one crossing.
50 ft. Bergen Av to Jackson Av, Myrtle to Orient.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the blocks of the Bergen section of Jersey City between Bergen Avenue at the top and Jackson Avenue at the bottom, from Orient Avenue on the left to the railroad cut on the right. Kearney Avenue and Ege Avenue run down the sheet and divide it into blocks 1983 and 1982, with a wedge-shaped block 1981 beside the railroad. The block between Orient and Kearney Avenues is built up with narrow lots of frame dwellings, with a manufacturer of metal goods and a number of flats near its middle and pink-coloured brick dwellings and stores along Orient Avenue and Jackson Avenue. The block between Kearney and Ege Avenues, with a large factory building of a manufacturer of medicines and digestives, drawn in pink, at its Bergen Avenue end, has frame dwellings and flats on both frontages and a few shops and sheds. East of Ege Avenue the lots narrow to a point along the broad diagonal right-of-way of the railroad, marked Plot T on block 1974 1/2, and the Jackson Avenue passenger station and an iron bridge stand at its lower end where the line crosses Jackson Avenue. Morton Place enters Bergen Avenue from the north as a short stub, and an iron bridge carries Bergen Avenue over the railroad at the top right. Sheet 21 adjoins on the left, sheets 26 and 28 are outlined below Jackson Avenue and sheet 23 beyond the railroad. Water pipes and street widths of 40 to 70 feet are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive in OpenStreetMap.
The detector found only one junction (Ege Avenue and Jackson Avenue): the arms of the other junctions are blocks with broken frontages or are not drawn on both sides, so four points are hand-picked.
The railroad cut is not used as control.
50 ft. Bergen Av to Jackson Av, Orient to the railroad; 1 detected and 4 hand-picked points.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the strip of Jersey City between Bergen Avenue at the top and Jackson Avenue at the bottom, along Virginia Avenue and Forrest, in the Bergen district. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. A wide cut of the Newark and New York Railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey) crosses the left side from Bergen Avenue to Jackson Avenue, where it reaches the Jackson Avenue Station with its covered steel footbridge, waiting room and concrete walk; the cut is crossed by an iron bridge at both streets, and the land west of it belongs to sheet 22. Between the cut and Virginia Avenue the lots are filled with a continuous row of frame dwellings of two storeys, with an open air theatre and its stage, a bottling works and a salon near Bergen Avenue, and Bernius Court entering from Virginia Avenue. East of Virginia Avenue the blocks hold scattered frame dwellings, three storey flats, McCabe's Express with its wagon shed, and at the Jackson Avenue end a block of brick stores and shops with a beer bottling works, electric motors and a drug store. Forrest runs down the right edge with the blocks of sheet 24 outlined beyond it. House numbers, water pipe sizes and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are marked, and block numbers 1978, 1979, 1980 and 1974 1/2 are printed. The upper left corner shows the outlines of sheets 19 and 20, and the lower edge those of sheets 24 and 28.
