Forrest is Forrest Street today.
Virginia Avenue jogs across Jackson Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two Virginia/Martin Luther King Drive nodes about 50 m apart and the sheet draws the north leg here.
Ege Avenue enters at the top left corner, where Bergen Avenue is cut by the sheet edge.
50 ft. Jackson Av to Bergen Av along Virginia and Forrest; Newark and New York RR cut, Jackson Av station.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 lies in the Bergen district of Jersey City and shows four blocks wide and three deep between Bergen Avenue at the top, Sackett in the middle and Jackson Avenue at the bottom, with Forrest, Oak, Union Street and Atlantic as the cross streets. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The Forrest and Oak frontages along the left are lined with frame dwellings of two and three storeys, flats of three and four storeys, and at the foot a row of stores. At the top left corner stands a large brick building, the Peoples Palace, with lodge rooms, bowling alleys, meeting rooms, an auditorium and gymnasium. The block between Oak and Union Street holds Public School No. 14 with its boiler house and a Manual Training School, with rows of brick flats and dwellings on both sides of it and stores, a bakery and a saloon along Jackson Avenue. The block east of Union Street is built with frame and brick dwellings, three storey flats, and a small green-coloured building with its own heating and lighting plant near the middle of the lower right block, with more dwellings along the Atlantic frontage on the right. Boyd Avenue enters Bergen Avenue from the top margin. House numbers, water pipe sizes, hydrants and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are marked, and block numbers 1975 to 1977 and 1958 and 1959 are printed. Sheets 19, 18, 23, 28, 27 and 29 are outlined around the edges.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive today (OpenStreetMap).
Forrest, Oak, Union, Sackett and Atlantic are Forrest Street, Oak Street, Union Street, Sackett Street and Atlantic Street today.
Sackett has no junction with Forrest in OpenStreetMap, and the sheet draws the blocks between Forrest and Oak without a street at that row.
The compass rose is printed at the top of the sheet above Bergen Avenue.
50 ft. Bergen, Sackett, Jackson Avs; Forrest to Atlantic.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 shows a district of mixed frame housing and small industry at the western edge of the Jersey City volume, from Jackson Avenue at the top to Ocean Avenue at the bottom, between Myrtle Avenue on the left and Orient Avenue on the right, with Grant and Claremont in between and Rose Avenue crossing the middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, and the left margin is lettered 'See Volume Nine'. The long block along Myrtle Avenue is mostly lots with three storey flats and two storey dwellings, a coal yard, a knitting mill (O. Havez), G. B. Gross and Sons grocers, a wood working plant with a large wood shed, and a kindling wood yard at the foot. Between Grant and Claremont stands Public School No. 29, with brick stores and shops along Jackson Avenue at the top, flats on both sides and a row of brick stores along Ocean Avenue at the bottom. East of Claremont the blocks are mainly frame dwellings with brick stores at the Jackson Avenue and Ocean Avenue ends and a doll factory (F. Kampff). Ocean Avenue runs diagonally across the lower part of the sheet and its junctions with Myrtle Avenue, Grant and Claremont are cut by it. The compass is drawn at the lower right, and sheets 21, 26, 34 and 35 are outlined around the edges. Block numbers 1987 to 1992 are printed.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive today; the stretch at Myrtle and Grant is Martin Luther King Jr. Drive in OpenStreetMap.
Ocean Avenue is drawn running diagonally across the lower part of the sheet.
50 ft. Jackson Av to Ocean Av, Myrtle to Orient.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the blocks of Jersey City between Jackson Avenue at the top and Ocean Avenue at the bottom, from Orient Avenue on the left to Ege Avenue on the right, with Rose Avenue and Hart cutting across and Kearney Avenue running the length of the sheet between two rows of blocks. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The Orient Avenue block is a long run of three storey flats and frame dwellings with a stair builder's shop (C. C. Clark and Son) and a patent stone works at the top, and a brick flat building at the foot. Between Kearney Avenue and Ege Avenue the blocks hold brick stores along Jackson Avenue and Ocean Avenue, a bakery and a plumber near Hart, dwellings, flats, and the Fire Department Engine Company No. 8 house. The block below Rose Avenue has flats, a paint shop, a boarding and carriage house with a large shed and frame shops with brick stores along Ocean Avenue. Ocean Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet obliquely and Carteret Avenue enters it from the bottom margin. Hydrants, fire alarm boxes, water pipe sizes and street widths of 50 to 70 feet are marked, and block numbers 1993 to 1996 are printed. Sheets 22, 25, 28, 35 and 36 are outlined around the edges.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive today (OpenStreetMap).
Hart is not a street in OpenStreetMap; the row it names is not part of today's street network.
Ege Avenue is shown reaching Ocean Avenue, which OpenStreetMap does not.
50 ft. Jackson Av to Ocean Av, Orient to Ege.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers a strip of Jersey City between Clinton Avenue at the top and Union at the bottom, turned about 90 degrees from the neighbouring sheets so that Jackson runs down the left side and Ocean Avenue down the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and the compass at the left points to the upper left. Bramhall Avenue and Atlantic cross the middle, and Monticello Avenue and Madison Avenue run between Clinton Avenue and Bramhall Avenue. The two upper blocks are built almost entirely with brick and frame flats and dwellings of three and four storeys, many on narrow lots, with a bakery at the foot of the block between Jackson and Monticello Avenue and a courtyard of flats near Clinton Avenue. The block between Bramhall Avenue and Atlantic has a row of brick dwellings along Bramhall Avenue, a drug store, the Church of the First Born, and a chapel, with frame dwellings and sheds behind. The lower block between Atlantic and Union holds flats, stores and saloons at the ends and an open air theatre with its stage and scenery near Ocean Avenue. Grand Street is lettered at the right where it joins Bramhall Avenue and Ocean Avenue. Block numbers 1951, 1952, 1961 and 1962 are printed. Water pipe sizes and street widths of 50, 60 and 70 feet are marked, and sheets 24, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32 and 38 are outlined around the sheet.
notes: Jackson is Martin Luther King Drive today; north of Bramhall Avenue the way is Jackson Street in OpenStreetMap.
Atlantic, Union and Ocean are Atlantic Street, Union Street and Ocean Avenue today.
The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheets 23 to 26 and 28 (rotation about -35 degrees against about 50 degrees).
50 ft. Clinton Av to Union, Jackson to Ocean; turned.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows five blocks of Jersey City stacked down the page, from Union at the top to Ege Avenue at the bottom, with Oak, Forrest and Virginia Avenue between, bounded by Jackson Avenue on the left and Ocean Avenue on the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north is towards the upper left, like sheet 27. A wide railroad cut of the Newark and New York Railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey) crosses the middle diagonally with Jackson Avenue Station and its footbridge at the left end, and the Forrest and Virginia Avenue blocks are split by it. The top blocks hold frame dwellings, three storey flats and brick stores, the Salem Baptist Church (Colored) with meeting rooms, brick pits and a laundry along Jackson Avenue. Between Oak and Forrest are the Bethel African Methodist Episcopal Church, moving pictures, and a long row of brick dwellings. Below the cut, the blocks along Virginia Avenue and Ege Avenue include the 8th Ward Republican Club, a liquor storage building, stores and drug store along Jackson Avenue and several three and four storey brick flats at the Ocean Avenue end. An iron bridge carries Ocean Avenue over the cut, and Hart is lettered at the bottom between sheet outlines. Block numbers 1971, 1972, 1974, 1974 1/2, 1997 and 1998 are printed, with the compass at the right edge. Sheets 23, 24, 26, 27, 36 and 37 are outlined around the edges.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive today (OpenStreetMap).
Union, Oak and Forrest are Union Street, Oak Street and Forrest Street today.
Virginia Avenue jogs across Jackson Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two nodes about 50 m apart, and this sheet draws the south leg along the Virginia Avenue block.
Hart Street is not a street in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheets 23 to 26 (rotation about -35 degrees).
50 ft. Union to Ege, Jackson to Ocean; turned.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the blocks of Jersey City between Bergen Avenue at the top and Jackson Avenue at the bottom, from Atlantic on the left to Clinton Avenue on the right, with Bramhall Avenue, Oxford Avenue, Sackett and Siedler as the main cross streets. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, and the grid fans out so that Bergen Avenue and Jackson Avenue are not parallel. Clendenny Avenue, Lexington Avenue, Oxford Avenue and Clinton Avenue enter Bergen Avenue from the top margin. The left blocks, along Atlantic and Bramhall Avenue, hold rows of two and three storey frame dwellings with a few flats, three blocks of cement block buildings, and brick dwellings and stores at the Jackson Avenue end. Between Bramhall Avenue and Clinton Avenue the upper blocks hold frame dwellings, flats and the American Patent Chair Company works; the block between Sackett and Siedler has a wagon shed, a livery stable, a garage and a long row of frame dwellings along Bramhall Avenue, and the lowest block has brick flats, dwellings and stores along Jackson Avenue. A short Bramhall Court enters from Bramhall Avenue. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants, water pipe sizes and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are marked, and block numbers 1953 to 1957 and 1960 are printed. Sheets 18, 24, 27 and 30 are outlined around the edges.
notes: Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive today; north of Bramhall Avenue the way is Jackson Street in OpenStreetMap.
Siedler is Seidler Street today (OpenStreetMap).
Atlantic and Sackett are Atlantic Street and Sackett Street today.
The grid is drawn fanned: Bergen Avenue and Jackson Avenue converge to the right.
50 ft. Bergen Av to Jackson Av, Atlantic to Clinton.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers a mixed residential and commercial strip of Jersey City's Lafayette district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Bergen Avenue crosses the top of the sheet on a slant, with Monticello Avenue closing the bottom, and Clinton Avenue and Communipaw Avenue run down the sheet with the long, narrow blocks between them numbered 1934 to 1937. Communipaw Avenue is a wide street with a block of its own on the east side, and Harrison Avenue forms the right-hand boundary, beyond which the margin reads 'See Volume Five'. Sackett, Siedler and Jackson Avenue cross between Clinton and Communipaw. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings and flats of two to three storeys, with brick rows on Siedler and Jackson, and many outbuildings and sheds at the rear of the lots. Commercial uses cluster on Communipaw Avenue: a steam laundry and a wagon builder near Bergen Avenue, the W. S. Everson and Co. storage warehouse (fireproof, reinforced concrete) with the Minford garage, the Crescent Electric Co., a bowling alley, a cigar factory, a livery and boarding stable and the E. A. Pyle livery stable. The Royal Arcanum Hall stands on Clinton Avenue at Siedler. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 to 80 feet are marked in the streets. The blocks of sheets 17, 27, 29 and 32 are outlined without detail around the edges.
notes: Siedler is Seidler Street in OpenStreetMap.
Jackson Avenue is Martin Luther King Drive today; no OpenStreetMap junction of that name matched on this sheet.
Sackett is not in OpenStreetMap at this position.
50 ft. Bergen to Monticello, Clinton, Communipaw, Harrison.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows a largely open triangular tract of Jersey City's Lafayette district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It is bounded by Madison Avenue along the top, Bramhall Avenue on the left, Clinton Avenue on the right and Arlington Avenue across the bottom, with Grand cutting diagonally from the upper left to the lower right and leaving block 1949 as a large triangle. Almost all of the sheet is empty ground. The built-up parts are a long row of three- and four-storey brick dwellings and flats facing Madison Avenue, a second row of dwellings and flats along the north side of Grand, a block of frame dwellings on Clinton Avenue, and a few scattered frame houses and outbuildings. The one large building is St. Patrick R. C. Church on Bramhall Avenue, drawn in blue as a hollow concrete or similar construction, with a 100 foot bell tower, steam heat and gas lighting. Block 1950 lies between Madison Avenue and Grand. Neighbouring sheets 27, 32, 33 and 38 are named in the margins. Street widths of 60 and 70 feet and 6 inch water pipes are marked, and a lot line runs across the empty land in the south.
notes: The church is lettered 'St. Patrick R. C. Church'.
Crescent Avenue is lettered only on a water-pipe note at the right edge.
Grand is Grand Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Madison, Bramhall, Clinton, Arlington; mostly open; St. Patrick R.C. Church.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the Communipaw Avenue district of Jersey City's Lafayette section, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Monticello Avenue runs across the top, then Madison Avenue and Crescent Avenue, and Arlington Avenue closes the bottom; Clinton Avenue bounds the left side. Communipaw Avenue and Harrison Avenue run down the right side and converge towards the bottom, with Harmon and Grand cutting diagonally through the lower blocks, which are numbered 1932 to 1941. Frame and brick dwellings and flats fill most blocks. Institutions and industry are notable: the Bergen Baptist Church on Monticello Avenue, the Monticello Theatre, Truck Company No. 5 of the fire department and the 9th Precinct police station on Communipaw Avenue, the Smooth-On Manufacturing Company, the New York and New Jersey Telephone Company exchange on Madison Avenue, The Jersey City Club on Clinton Avenue and a coal yard at Madison and Communipaw. In the south a large post office building, J. H. Ficken's storage warehouse and the Junction Motor Company garage appear. The sheet sits between sheets 27, 30, 31 and 33, which are named at its margins. Water pipes and widths of 50 to 70 feet are marked.
notes: Park Street is lettered only on a water-pipe note at the lower right.
Arlington Avenue/Communipaw Avenue and Arlington Avenue/Harmon junctions were not detected; Harmon and Grand are Harmon Street and Grand Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Monticello to Arlington, Communipaw and Harrison.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 shows the district east of Bramhall Avenue in Jersey City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Communipaw Avenue runs across the top beneath a margin marked 'See Volume Five', with Harmon and Mc Dougall Street crossing below it, Arlington Avenue at the left, Randolph Avenue and Garfield Avenue running down the sheet, and Bramhall Avenue across the bottom. The blocks are numbered 1942 to 1949. Small frame dwellings and flats fill the blocks near Communipaw and Harmon, with a triangular block of brick and frame buildings between Grand and Communipaw Avenue. Block 1945 holds frame dwellings and flats, and farther south there are rows of flats on Randolph Avenue. A Public Service Railway transforming station and an abandoned gas holder stand east of Randolph Avenue. The southern half is occupied by the greenhouses of Peter Henderson and Co., seedsmen, with a work shop and packing house along their north side, and the fertiliser and seed warehouse of the same firm at the right edge beside Garfield Avenue, drawn against a railroad or canal line at the sheet's edge. The sheet is drawn with north towards the upper left and lies between sheets 32, 38, 39 and 49.
notes: The grid on this sheet is turned about 85 degrees from sheet 32; the fitted rotation is -29 degrees against 55 on its neighbours.
Mc Dougall Street is McDougall Street in OpenStreetMap; Prescott Street and Summit Avenue are lettered at the top margin and were not read at full resolution.
50 ft. Communipaw to Bramhall, Randolph and Garfield; Peter Henderson greenhouses; turned.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 is the western end of the Claremont and Randolph blocks of Jersey City's Lafayette section, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Ocean Avenue forms the top boundary, then Clerk, Arlington Avenue and Randolph Avenue run across the sheet, with Garfield Avenue cutting diagonally at the bottom. Claremont Avenue bounds the right side and Myrtle Avenue the left, running on a slant, beyond which the margin reads 'See Volume Nine'. Blocks 2012 to 2015 are filled with frame dwellings, with brick houses facing Ocean Avenue and a row of larger houses on the north side of Arlington Avenue. Churches are the principal institutions: Claremont Presbyterian Church at Ocean and Claremont, the Holy Cross parish hall and a Christ Episcopal church (drawn diagonally) near Claremont Avenue. Greenhouses and a few sheds stand in the south, in block 2015 on Randolph and Garfield. Street widths of 60 to 70 feet, water pipes and hydrants are marked. The sheet adjoins sheet 35 on the right and sheets 25 and 42 above and below.
notes: Clerk is Clerk Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Christ Episcopal church name was read at medium confidence.
Grant Avenue and Caven Pt Avenue are lettered at the top and bottom margins.
50 ft. Myrtle to Claremont, Ocean to Garfield.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows a residential district of the Lafayette and Bergen section of Jersey City: the three blocks between Ocean Avenue at the top and Randolph Avenue at the bottom, bounded by Claremont Avenue on the west and Carteret Avenue on the east, with Clerk and Arlington Avenue crossing between them. The blocks are filled almost entirely with frame dwellings of two to three storeys on narrow lots, many marked as flats, with stores at a few corners and a handful of brick dwellings in rows along Ocean Avenue and Clerk. Outbuildings and sheds stand at the rear of many lots, and the deep lots leave open yards along the middle of each block. Orient Avenue and Kearney Avenue are drawn as short stubs entering Ocean Avenue from the top margin, where the blocks of sheets 25 and 26 are outlined without detail; the blocks east of Carteret Avenue and west of Claremont Avenue belong to sheets 36 and 34, and those below Randolph Avenue to sheet 42. Water pipes, their diameters and street widths of 50 to 70 feet are marked in every street, with fire hydrants at the corners. House numbers run along every frontage, and block numbers 2009 to 2011 are printed in the blocks. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Clerk is Clerk Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Pilot. Ocean Av to Randolph Av between Claremont Av and Carteret Av; Clerk St, Arlington Av.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 lies east of sheet 35 in Jersey City's Lafayette section, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Ocean Avenue runs across the top, with the stubs of Ege Avenue and Virginia Avenue entering it from the margin, and Clerk, Arlington Avenue and Randolph Avenue run across the sheet below, with Carteret Avenue on the left. The right third is cut by the Newark and New York railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey), drawn in a cutting crossed by iron bridges, and Forest runs beside it at the right edge, where the blocks of sheets 37 and 41 are named. Blocks 1999 to 2001 are filled with frame dwellings and flats, with a bank and shops on Ocean Avenue at Carteret Avenue (Claremont Bank), the Bowne Memorial M. E. Church on the north side of Clerk and a row of brick houses on Ocean Avenue. Randolph Avenue turns diagonally to the south-east and is lined on both sides by dwellings on narrow lots in fan-shaped blocks, ending at a railroad depot beside the cut. Water pipes, hydrants and widths of 60 to 70 feet are marked.
notes: Forest is Forrest Street in OpenStreetMap; sheet 37 prints it Forrest.
Clerk is Clerk Street in OpenStreetMap.
Control is four points along Carteret Avenue and one on Ocean Avenue; rotation agrees with sheet 35.
50 ft. Carteret to Forest, rail cut; 4 of 5 points on Carteret Av, weak.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 lies east of sheet 36 in Jersey City's Lafayette section, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Ocean Avenue crosses the top, with Oak Street entering it from the margin, and Clerk, Minerva, Arlington Avenue and Randolph Avenue cross the sheet below; Forrest runs down the left side beside the Newark and New York railroad (Central Railroad of New Jersey), crossed by iron bridges, and Union forms the right boundary. Blocks 1968 to 1973 are filled with frame dwellings and flats, among them a long brick row on Union Street at Ocean Avenue, a row of dwellings along Arlington Avenue, and many outbuildings. The railroad cut occupies the lower left, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey passenger depot beside it. On Randolph Avenue the Greenfield Conduit Manufacturing Company's factory and shipping rooms, for galvanized conduit pipe, take up most of block 1968. A plumber's shop and a few shops stand on Ocean Avenue. Widths of 50 to 60 feet, water pipes and hydrants are marked; the neighbouring sheets 28, 36, 38 and 40 are named at the margins.
notes: Forrest and Union are Forrest Street and Union Street in OpenStreetMap; sheet 36 prints Forrest as Forest.
Minerva Street/Union Street was rejected as 7 m off; Minerva Street may be realigned.
Clerk Street is lettered a second time to the west, across the railroad.
50 ft. Forrest to Union, rail cut; Minerva St left out (7 m).

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows a block-and-a-half wide strip of the Lafayette district of Jersey City between Ocean Avenue at the top and Randolph Avenue at the bottom, bounded by Union on the left and Bramhall Avenue on the right, with Clerk and Arlington Avenue crossing between them. The upper block (number 1963) is occupied at its east end by St. Patrick's Parochial Building, a brick school with gymnasium, class rooms, theatre, bowling alleys and pool room, and by St. Patrick's Convent; a long row of brick dwellings runs along Union and across the Ocean Avenue frontage, and the Wm. Roche dry battery works stands among frame dwellings in the middle of the block. The block between Clerk and Arlington Avenue (1964) holds frame dwellings and flats on both fronts, a row of brick houses on Arlington Avenue, and S. Goldberg's carpet slipper works with a storage building. The lowest block (1965) is filled with frame dwellings, a brick row near Randolph Avenue, and a few auto sheds. Neighbouring sheets are noted by number: 27 above, 37 to the left, 31 and 33 to the right and 40 below. Streets are 50 to 60 feet wide with 6 inch water pipes, and a diagonal Grand Street is seen entering at the top right corner. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and its north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Clerk is Clerk Street and Union is Union Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Union, Bramhall, Ocean to Randolph.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers an industrial strip in the Communipaw district of Jersey City along the east bank of the Morris Canal. Communipaw Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with Manning Avenue entering from the north, and Woodward runs down the right-hand side to meet Bramhall Avenue near the bottom right. The sheet is turned about a quarter turn from the neighbouring sheets, so that north points toward the upper left. The left third is the canal, its tow path and the Newark and New York Railroad, with a coal yard and trestle beside them. The centre is occupied by the Prentiss Tool and Supply Co. warehouse, the P. Derby and Co. chair factory and the extensive American Radiator Company warehouses, an old foundry used to store radiators (plot A, block 1948 1/2). In the upper right block (2040) are the W. Ames spike and bolt works, with its rolling mill, spike shop, machine shop and storage of bolts and spikes, together with a scrap iron shed, a row of flats on Communipaw Avenue and the Christ Evangelical Lutheran Church with its rectory. Rail spurs curve through the yard. Much of the right side and the lower right is open ground. Adjoining sheets named on the margins are 49, 50, 53, 33 and 40. Scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Woodward is Woodward Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions; the sheet is turned about 100 degrees from sheet 38.
50 ft. Turned industrial strip on the Morris Canal; 3 points (2 hand-picked), low confidence.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 lies on the line of the Morris Canal in the Lafayette and Communipaw districts of Jersey City. The upper part shows Randolph Avenue running across the top with Union and Garfield Avenue crossing it; Garfield Avenue bends from a diagonal on the left to run straight across the middle, and Bramhall Avenue closes the right edge. The block between Randolph and Garfield (1966) is filled with frame dwellings and flats with a laundry and a saloon, while the Knapp Chemical Company and the Builders Hoist and Machine Company occupy the corner by Union. A coal yard (O'Connor Bros.) and coal pockets lie against the Newark and New York Railroad on the left. Below Garfield Avenue the lots (1948) back onto the Morris Canal, which crosses the sheet from left to right with its tow path. South of the canal lies the open yard of the American Radiator Company (2037, report on sheet 39), crossed by railroad tracks, with a long warehouse, sheds and a repair shop for contractors' locomotives (Jas. S. Braden). Woodward runs diagonally across the lower part. The adjoining sheets are 37, 38, 33, 39, 41 and 54. Scale is 50 feet to an inch; north is toward the upper right.
notes: Union is Union Street and Woodward is Woodward Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Bramhall Avenue / Woodward junction at the bottom right was hand-picked and agrees with the fit to four detected junctions.
50 ft. Morris Canal, Garfield Av.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows the Garfield Avenue district of Jersey City between Randolph Avenue on the left and the Morris Canal on the right, turned so that north points toward the upper left. Carteret Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet. Randolph Avenue is a curved street along the west side with a row of frame dwellings and flats; Garfield Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs diagonally up the middle from Carteret Avenue toward the railroad. The blocks between them (2002) are deep narrow lots, with a few frame houses at the lower end, the James Spence Iron Foundry and the Cochran Chemical Co., makers of water proof compositions, at the top by the Newark and New York Railroad, which crosses the upper left diagonally. East of Garfield Avenue, Jane Street and Commercial, which are no longer streets, bound blocks 2005 and 2004, which hold the Carbonoid Mfg. Co. paper treating plant and many vacant lots. The Natural Products Refining Co. (block 2003), makers of bichromate of soda, with its numbered buildings and tanks, stands near the railroad. The Morris Canal and its tow path run diagonally down the right, with Valley and Woodward (not opened) beyond, and Public Service Gas Co. ground at the right. Adjoining sheets are 36, 40, 42 and 55. Scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Commercial, Jane and Valley no longer exist; Woodward is Woodward Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from two junctions only (helmert): low confidence.
50 ft. Turned; Carteret Av only (2 junctions, helmert), low confidence.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 shows a narrow district of Jersey City east of Randolph Avenue between Carteret Avenue at the top and Claremont Avenue and Caven Point Avenue at the bottom, turned so that north points toward the upper left. Garfield Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs diagonally from Carteret Avenue at the top to Caven Point Avenue at the bottom. The long block between Randolph and Garfield (2008) is built up on the Randolph frontage with frame dwellings and flats, while its centre is the James Craig works, manufacturers of engines, with an engine house and office. The strip east of Garfield Avenue and west of Commercial (2007) is divided into narrow lots with only a few buildings near Carteret Avenue and a saloon at Caven Point Avenue, and the next strip east of Commercial (2006) is all unbuilt lots back to the Morris Canal and its tow path. Valley runs along the far side of the canal. Halladay Street enters at the lower right. Below Claremont Avenue is block 34 with a note See Volume Nine. The adjoining sheets are 35, 41, 34 and 56. Scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Commercial and Valley no longer exist; the rest are on their modern lines.
A margin note reads See Volume Nine.
50 ft. Turned; Garfield Av, Carteret, Caven Point.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 shows the east edge of the Communipaw district of Jersey City, where Grand runs down the right side of the sheet, with Center Street and Bates Street entering from the right and Pacific Avenue, 80 feet wide, crossing diagonally from the upper left to meet it. The sheet is turned so that north points to the right and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. A wedge of land between Pacific Avenue and the National Docks Railroad is occupied by the L. Wertheim Coal and Coke Co., with coke and charcoal sheds, a trestle track on a curve and coal pockets (block 2143). Along the south side of Pacific Avenue are the Hennepin Mills flour storage and N. Drake's ice platform, and across the lower part spread the yards of the Lehigh Valley Railroad (block 2144), with an open platform and the Lehigh Valley Railroad freight depot, office and produce shed. The Morris Canal comes in from the upper left and runs down the left side to meet Mill Creek, which crosses the bottom. Merseles Street is named at the top right. The right edge carries the margin note See Volume Five and the bottom See Volume One. Adjoining sheets are 45, 66 and 44.
notes: Grand is Grand Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from three nearly collinear junctions along Grand (helmert): low confidence.
50 ft. Turned; Grand St and Pacific Av, rail yards; 3 nearly collinear points, low confidence; Merseles left out (drawn junction 455 ft from Center, modern 213 ft).

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 covers the east side of the Communipaw district of Jersey City where Johnstone Avenue, Grand and Manning Avenue meet, with its north arrow pointing to the upper left. Two long wedge-shaped blocks run up the sheet: the left one between Grand and Manning Avenue (2086), with a continuous row of frame flats and stores on Grand and Public School No. 19 at its foot, and the right one between Manning Avenue and Woodward (2087), a block of frame flats and dwellings with a Negro church (D. 2nd) and rows of lots running back to the rear lanes, with brick dwellings along Woodward. At the top the blocks narrow to a point where Grand meets Woodward, with saloons and flats on the corner. Johnstone Avenue crosses the lower part, and below it are the Woodhouse and Co. window frame and moulding works, the Newark Industrial Home and Mission, and other works near Bishop and Carbon. The Morris Canal, with its tow path and an iron bridge, crosses the lower right between two streets named Carbon. Side streets named on the margin to the left are Fairmount Avenue, Fremont Street, Prior Street, Bishop Street and Johnstone Avenue, and Harold Place at the right. The left margin carries the note See Volume Five. Adjoining sheets are 45, 47, 49 and 43. Scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue and Grand is Grand Street in OpenStreetMap.
Grand and Johnston Avenue meet at two offset junctions (about 31 m apart); both are used as control points.
50 ft. Grand, Manning, Johnstone; turned.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 covers an industrial and lumber-yard district of Jersey City's Hudson City section, lying between Woodward Street on the west, Pacific Avenue on the east and Johnstone Avenue along the bottom of the sheet, with Van Horne and Halladay streets running up the page between them. The Morris Canal crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right in a broad diagonal, with the strip marked Carbon laid out along its edges. The largest feature is the Charles R. Partridge Lumber Company yard (block 2100), drawn as dashed lumber piles over open ground north of the canal and continuing south of it along Van Horne Street. The Hardwood Lumber piles lie to its east. At the top the National Docks Railway runs in from the upper right past the coal pockets and trestle of the E. L. Young Co. and Lehigh Valley Coal Co. Along the west edge are rows of frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with H. J. Heinz Co. (storage of groceries) at Harold Place, and further south the Boston Cocoa Mfg Co. and Josiah Partridge and Sons, and the Columbia Water Co. making carbonated waters near Ash and Pacific Avenue. The compass shows north towards the upper left. Block numbers 2085 1/2 (plot A), 2088, 2089, 2090, 2091, 2099 and 2100 are printed. Adjoining sheets 43, 44, 46 and 47 are named in the margins and "See Volume Five" is printed at the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Carbon is lettered along both edges of the Morris Canal strip; no street of that name survives here (Carbon Place is a different modern street).
Harold Place is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The street grid fits a rotation of about -47 degrees (north towards the upper left), sheets 46 to 48 about +43 degrees.
50 ft. Lumber yards and canal, Woodward to Pacific, Johnstone.

sheet-46-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 46, a manufacturing and warehouse district of Jersey City east of Lafayette. It is bounded by Pacific Avenue along the top, Johnstone Avenue down the left edge and Garrabrant along the bottom, with Ash running up the page near the middle and Whiton, Pine and Monitor crossing from left to right. The blocks are numbered 2092, 2093, 2094, 2095, 2097 and 2098. Near the top, rows of brick stores and frame dwellings front Pacific Avenue, with sheds and yards behind. R. Hillier's Son Company and the Eureka Packing Co. (steam packing) stand beside Whiton Street, and the F. W. Bussing Co. (cocoa nuts) occupies a large plant between Ash Street and the railroad. Block 2094, between Pine and Monitor, is platted into narrow lots with no buildings. On the right a broad diagonal band of tracks, marked National Docks Railway, cuts across the sheet from the lower left to the upper right and takes the east end of every cross street. Below Monitor Street a lumber yard and sheds stand beside the tracks, and the left edge of the area at Garrabrant carries rows of flats. North is towards the upper right. A separate block east of the heavy line at the lower right, with its own compass and the Mersereau Metal Bed Company foundry, is drawn on the sheet as part 2 and is not part of this map. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue and Garrabrant is Garabrant Street in OpenStreetMap.
The detector reported the drawn National Docks Branch about 11 m from its modern line.
Part 2, the area east of the heavy line at the lower right (Mersereau Metal Bed Company, Johnstone Avenue and Garrabrant), has its own compass and is not georeferenced here.
50 ft. Part 1 main (Pacific to Garrabrant, Johnstone to National Docks Ry). Part 2: block behind the heavy line at lower right (Mersereau Metal Bed Co.), drawn displaced, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: block at lower right behind a heavy line (Mersereau Metal Bed Co. foundry, Johnstone Av and Garrabrant) (drawn displaced from the main part; no street junction of its own; needs step 6b: carried points from sheets 65 or 66).

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows a residential and light-industrial strip of Jersey City's Lafayette district, between Maple Street on the west and Johnstone Avenue on the east, from Manning Avenue at the top to Pacific Avenue at the bottom. Woodward, Van Horne and Halladay run across the sheet from left to right. At the left edge, outside the drawn blocks, the vertical lettering Lafayette Park marks the edge of the park shown on sheet 50. The upper blocks (2078 and 2079) are laid out in narrow lots, most of them still without buildings, and the Morris Canal crosses the top right corner in a diagonal, with the strip lettered Carbon beside it and block 2085 1/2 plot A beyond. Below Van Horne Street the blocks (2077 and 2076) are built up with frame dwellings and flats along the street frontages, small sheds at the rear, and a few brick buildings, with a lodge hall among the buildings on Halladay Street. Blocks to the east, across Johnstone Avenue, belong to sheet 45 and sheet 44. Neighbouring sheet numbers 49, 50, 51, 45 and 48 are printed in the margins. The compass at the upper left shows north towards the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Maple is Maple Street.
Woodward and Manning Avenue end at the Morris Canal strip (Carbon) on this sheet.
The street grid fits a rotation of about +43 degrees (north towards the upper right), the same as sheets 46 and 48 and the opposite sense to sheets 45, 49, 50 and 51.
50 ft. Maple to Johnstone, Manning to Pacific, Morris Canal.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 shows four blocks of Jersey City's Lafayette district, between Maple Street on the west and Johnstone Avenue on the east, from Pacific Avenue at the top to Garrabrant at the bottom. Whiton, Pine and Monitor cross the sheet from left to right. The blocks are numbered 2072 to 2075. The top block (2075) is densely built with brick and frame stores and dwellings along Pacific Avenue and a hall and battery club building at its east end. Block 2074 has a long row of narrow brick buildings fronting Whiton Street, frame flats and dwellings elsewhere and the Lafayette Hall saloon at the corner of Johnstone Avenue. Block 2073 holds frame dwellings and flats along Pine and Monitor Streets and the wagon shed of the United States Express Co. At the bottom, block 2072 is filled by the United States Express Co. stables (fire-proof construction, with hollow tile walls and steel girders) and by the furniture works of Josiah Partridge and Sons Co. facing Garrabrant. The surrounding blocks to the east and west are outlined and numbered 46 and 51 and 52, and the sheet below is 65. A scale bar and the compass, with north towards the upper right, are shown. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue and Garrabrant is Garabrant Street in OpenStreetMap; Maple is Maple Street.
50 ft. Pacific to Garrabrant, Maple to Johnstone.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 lies on the Morris Canal in the Lafayette district of Jersey City, between Grand Avenue and Garfield Avenue on the west and Manning Avenue on the east, with Communipaw Avenue along the bottom. The canal sweeps from the lower left to the upper right across the whole sheet, with the lettering Morris Canal along it, and the strip beside it marked Carbon. East of the canal is the large works of the Whitlock Cordage Co., manufacturers of hemp rope, drawn in pink fire-proof and brick construction with numbered buildings (hemp store house, rope making and balling, finished goods, main building, tar house, store house, repair shop, office) inside a dashed property line, and an engine house and boiler plant at its north end. South of it is the long mill-construction building of the Riegel Sack Co., makers of cloth bags. On the west bank of the canal, along Grand and Garfield Avenues, are the Baldwin Lumber Co. yard, a coal yard with pink and yellow sheds, Manning, Maxwell and Moore hardware and machine stock, and a few frame dwellings and flats. Blocks 2058, 2058 1/2 (plot A) and 2080 are numbered. The vertical lettering Volume Five on the left margin refers to the neighbouring volume, and the adjoining sheets 33, 39, 44, 47 and 50 are named. The compass at the upper left shows north towards the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Communipaw Avenue is 60 feet wide here and its edges are faint, so Communipaw Avenue at Manning Avenue was hand-picked on the middle of its drawn edges.

The junction of Garfield and Communipaw Avenues, hand-picked from the drawn lines, lies about 10 m from the modern node when the part is placed from Manning Avenue at the sheet's scale; the part is anchored on one junction and is low confidence.
Summit Avenue is drawn meeting Garfield Avenue north of Communipaw Avenue; OpenStreetMap has it meeting Communipaw Avenue.
The reading of State Street, Bishop and Maple is medium confidence (small lettering).
50 ft. Morris Canal, Whitlock Cordage, Riegel Sack; one hand-picked point plus 3 seam points carried from sheet 50; low confidence.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 shows Lafayette Park and the blocks around it in the Lafayette district of Jersey City. The park, blocks 2064 and 2065, fills the upper left of the sheet between Maple on the north, Lafayette on the south and Manning Avenue on the west. It is drawn with dashed paths radiating from a central wading pool with a small pavilion, and is lettered Lafayette Park. The blocks to the east, between Van Horne and Halladay, are filled with rows of frame and brick flats on narrow lots, with a Baptist church (negro) on block 2066 and a fire department house, engine company number 10, on block 2054 near Communipaw Avenue. Below Lafayette, block 2055 between Woodward and Van Horne has pink flats along its east side and a large unbuilt portion, block 2056 between Manning Avenue and Woodward is mostly platted lots with a few sheds, and at the upper left the Whitlock Cordage Co. has a small storage house. Communipaw Avenue runs along the bottom, with bowling alleys and flats near Halladay. The compass at upper left shows north towards the upper left. Adjoining sheets 47, 49, 51, 53 and 39 are named in the margins. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Maple and Lafayette are Maple Street and Lafayette Street in OpenStreetMap.
Communipaw Avenue at Woodward Street and at Manning Avenue was measured from edges narrower than the parcels' 60 feet; residuals were under 2 m.
50 ft. Lafayette Park and blocks.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 shows six blocks of the Lafayette district of Jersey City, between Halladay Street on the west and Pine Street on the east, and from Maple at the top to Communipaw Avenue at the bottom, with Lafayette crossing the middle. Pacific Avenue and Whiton run up the page between the blocks. The blocks are numbered 2051 to 2053 below Lafayette and 2067 to 2069 above it. They are built mainly with frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots with outbuildings at the rear. Notable buildings are All Saints Rectory and the All Saints School and Lyceum, Lafayette M. E. Church and its chapel, Public School No. 13, the Lafayette Reformed Church, and a row of pink brick dwellings named Breadalbane Terrace at the foot of block 2067. A lumber yard and sheds, and a few stores, stand along Communipaw Avenue. Fire alarm boxes and hydrants mark the street corners. Neighbouring sheets 47 and 48 are above, 53 and 57 below, 50 at the left and 52 at the right. North is towards the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Maple and Lafayette are Maple Street and Lafayette Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Halladay to Pine, Maple to Communipaw.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers the Communipaw district of Jersey City between Maple at the top and Communipaw Avenue at the bottom, with Lafayette crossing the middle of the sheet. Pine runs down the left side, Monitor down the middle and Garrabrant along the right edge, which is drawn as a boundary with the note 'not opened' beside it. The two blocks on the left, numbered 2070 and 2050, are lined with frame dwellings, flats and a few stores, with a wagon works, a beer bottling works and a liquor rectifier's premises mixed in at the lower block. East of Monitor the upper block (2071) is a row of frame dwellings and flats backing onto a wood yard, with an independent electric plant and a concrete carpenter's shop near the middle. The whole lower half of the east block (2049) is taken by the American Type Founders Company, a semi-fireproof brass and type foundry drawn in pink, with six numbered bays, casting rooms, a shipping department, boiler and engine room, and a printed note on its watchmen, fire alarm, power and water supply in the lower right corner. Neighbouring sheets are named at the margins: 48 above, 51 to the left, 58 below and 65 to the right. Suydam Avenue is lettered running off the bottom edge. Water pipes (6 inch and 12 inch) and street widths of 60 feet are marked at every crossing. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose near the top right; north points to the upper left.
notes: Garrabrant Street is Garabrant Street in OpenStreetMap; no junction of it with Communipaw Avenue survives, so it was not used for control.
Maple, Lafayette, Monitor and Pine are Maple Street, Lafayette Street, Monitor Street and Pine Street today.
The sheet is turned so that north is towards the upper left (rotation about -47 degrees).
50 ft. Maple to Communipaw, Pine to Garrabrant; American Type Founders.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 shows three blocks of the Communipaw district of Jersey City lying between Communipaw Avenue at the top and Bramhall Avenue at the bottom, bounded on the left by Woodward and on the right by Pacific Avenue, with Van Horne and Halladay between them. The left block (2041) is dominated on its west side by the works of the New York Standard Watch Company (the Keystone Watch Case Company), a large pink fireproof complex fitted with automatic sprinklers, with its own gas engine and tank house and a mutual risk admittance-refused note; the rest of the block is rows of frame dwellings along Van Horne and Woodward, with an open yard, a water tank and an oil tank at the rear. The middle block (2042) is almost all two and three storey frame dwellings and flats, with a bakery, a Chinese laundry and stores facing Communipaw Avenue. The right block (2043) holds All Saints R.C. Church with its bell tower, St. Agnes Chapel, the rectory, Public School No. 22 and a row of brick dwellings along Pacific Avenue, with a contractor's yard near the bottom. Water pipes of 6 and 16 inches are marked in the streets, and street widths of 60 and 80 feet are given. The adjoining sheets are 50 above, 51 above right, 54 below, 39 on the left and 57 on the right. The scale is 50 feet to an inch and north is towards the upper left.
notes: Woodward, Van Horne and Halladay are Woodward Street, Van Horne Street and Halladay Street in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is turned so that north is towards the upper left (rotation about -47 degrees).
50 ft. Communipaw to Bramhall; watch case works, school.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 continues south from sheet 53 and covers the blocks between Bramhall Avenue at the top and Forrest at the bottom, from Woodward on the left to Pacific Avenue on the right, with Van Horne and Halladay between. Frame dwellings and flats line the upper halves of the three blocks (numbers 2036, 2035 and 2034), with a bowling alley and hall near Bramhall Avenue, two saloons on the right block and a zucker refinery for brewing purposes (L. Neve) at the left. A wide railroad corridor crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right, drawn with the Newark and New York Railroad (Central R.R. of New Jersey) tracks, a railroad station and a railroad watchman's shed, and the coal pockets and coal yards of McConnell Coal Company and Hauck Brothers along it. South of the tracks, blocks 2029 and 2030 hold Moore Brothers Publishing Company, a row of brick dwellings on Halladay, the varnish, oil and bronze powder works of Geo. H. Aspinwall Inc., the Flost Veneer Seating Company with its planing mill, and a tarpaulin manufactory (A. Sackett) beside the railroad. Block 2028 at lower left is left empty. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet and 6 inch water pipes are marked. The neighbouring sheets are 53 above, 55 below, 40 to the left and 57 and 61 to the right. The scale is 50 feet to an inch, north to the upper left.
notes: Forrest is Forrest Street today; the railroad corridor has been rebuilt and its modern line differs from the drawn tracks.
The sheet is turned so that north is towards the upper left (rotation about -47 degrees).
50 ft. Bramhall to Forrest, railroad corridor, coal yards.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 shows the southern end of the Communipaw district of Jersey City, from Forrest at the top to Carteret Avenue at the bottom. Woodward is lettered 'not opened' on the left, and the Morris Canal runs diagonally across the lower left corner with Valley, a narrow strip along its edge, drawn beside it. The upper part of the sheet is taken by the plant of the Public Service Gas Company (Consumers Gas Company), marked 'admittance refused, plant not in operation', in blocks 2026 and 2025: pink brick buildings along the Forrest side, two gas holders, two oil tanks and a few small structures stand in an otherwise open yard. Below the plant Van Horne is drawn as an open street running to Carteret Avenue, with long narrow platted lots on either side and short pairs of lots at the ends. To the right Halladay runs the full height of the sheet and block 2024 between Halladay and Pacific Avenue is divided into narrow lots, with only a saloon and three small buildings built. The railroad corridor of the Newark and New York Railroad (Central R.R. of New Jersey) enters the top left corner. Water pipes of 6 and 16 inches and street widths of 60 and 80 feet are marked. Neighbouring sheets are 54 above, 56 below, 41 to the left and 60 to the right. The scale is 50 feet to an inch and north is towards the upper left.
notes: Woodward is printed 'not opened' on this sheet.

Halladay and Van Horne south of Forrest do not survive as streets in OpenStreetMap, so only Forrest / Halladay, Forrest / Pacific Avenue and Carteret Avenue / Pacific Avenue were available as control.
The Morris Canal and Valley are gone.
50 ft. Forrest to Carteret, gas works, Morris Canal; exact 3-point fit.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers the empty southern edge of the Communipaw district of Jersey City, between Carteret Avenue at the top and Caven Point Avenue at the bottom. Halladay and Pacific Avenue run the length of the sheet, with Van Horne lettered at the top left, and the Morris Canal crosses diagonally from upper left to lower centre with its towpath and the strip called Valley running alongside it. Blocks 2016 and 2017 are platted into long narrow lots, a few at the ends turned to run the other way, but almost nothing is built: a few small dwellings and a saloon stand at the foot of the left block beside the canal, and the rest of the ground is blank. The block to the left of the canal (42) and the sheet to the lower right are other sheets, and a box at the bottom reads 'See Volume Nine', where the district continues. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet and 6, 8 and 16 inch water pipes are marked at the crossings. Neighbouring sheets are 55 above, 42 left, 59 right. The scale is 50 feet to an inch and north is towards the upper left; the compass rose is near the top right.
notes: Only two junctions (Carteret Avenue / Pacific Avenue and Caven Point Avenue / Pacific Avenue), both on Pacific Avenue, survive in the modern street network, so the placement is a two-point helmert and low confidence.
Halladay and Van Horne south of Forrest and the Morris Canal no longer exist.
50 ft. Carteret to Caven Point, mostly empty lots; 2-point helmert, low confidence.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 lies to the east of sheet 53 and shows the blocks between Pacific Avenue on the left and Pine on the right, with Whiton between them, running from Communipaw Avenue at the top down to the railroad corridor near the bottom. The left block (2044) is lined along Pacific Avenue and Whiton with brick and frame dwellings and flats, with a row of brick dwellings facing Communipaw Avenue, and the lower third is occupied by The Boynton Furnace Company, a manufacturer of furnaces, boilers and ranges, with a foundry, moulding shed, pattern storage and mounting rooms and a note on its watchmen and fire protection at the left margin. The right block (2045) holds frame and brick dwellings and flats along Whiton and Pine with sheds and a wagon shed at the rear. Boltwood, a narrow street about 20 feet wide, leaves Pine to the right and Bramhall Avenue is lettered at the lower left. The Newark and New York Railroad (Central R.R. of New Jersey) crosses the lower right corner with several tracks and curves. Water pipes of 6, 12 and 16 inches are marked and the streets are given as 55 and 60 feet wide. Neighbouring sheets are 51 above, 53 left, 58 right and 54 and 61 below. The scale is 50 feet to an inch and north is towards the upper left.
notes: Whiton, Pine and Pacific Avenue are Whiton Street, Pine Street and Pacific Avenue today.
The Boltwood Street / Pine Street control point was hand-picked on the drawn corner.
50 ft. Communipaw to Pacific, Whiton, Pine; Boynton Furnace.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 shows the eastern end of the Communipaw district of Jersey City, from Communipaw Avenue at the top to the railroad corridors below. Pine is lettered down the left margin with Boltwood leaving it to the right, and Monitor, Garrabrant and the diagonal Suydam Avenue run south from Communipaw Avenue. The left part is a block (2046) of frame dwellings and flats along Pine and Boltwood, backing onto the large works of The Hall Lace Company and H. S. Hall Lace Company, manufacturers of laces and veilings, with a weaving plant, a drafting room, winding and bobbin rooms, an independent electric plant and a printed note on the firm's watchmen and fire protection at the foot. Holloway Dyeing Company stands at the left of the works. Between Suydam Avenue and the tracks block 2047 holds rows of brick and frame dwellings and the paint and varnish works of William T. Baker Company, Inc. The right half of the sheet is railroad land: the Newark and New York Railroad (Central R.R. of New Jersey), the Lehigh Valley R.R. and the Central R.R. of New Jersey yard with its many tracks, a small structure marked as a depot building, and an iron bridge carrying Communipaw Avenue across the tracks at the top right. Blocks 52, 57, 61, 63, 64 and 65 are neighbouring sheets. The scale is 50 feet to an inch and north is towards the upper left.
notes: Garrabrant Street is Garabrant Street in OpenStreetMap; it has no surviving junction with Communipaw Avenue.
The left edge cuts Pine, so Communipaw Avenue / Pine Street rests on one drawn side; placement uses Communipaw Avenue, Suydam Avenue and two hand-picked points and is low confidence.
50 ft. Communipaw, Hall Lace, rail yards; 4 points nearly on one line.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 lies at the south-western edge of the Jersey City map, where Pacific Avenue, drawn across the top of the sheet, meets Caven Point Avenue at the left margin and Carteret Avenue at the right. The only built ground is the strip of lots on the south side of Pacific Avenue, most of it occupied by the New York Foundry Co., whose frame and brick foundry building with its cupolas is coloured yellow, with a small office and sheds beside it; the notes record three watchmen, no clock, and electric power and lights. A short 30 foot street, Whiton, is drawn at the lower right of the block beside Carteret Avenue. Below the foundry the sheet is almost entirely railroad right of way: wide bands of parallel tracks of the Lehigh Valley R. R., the Central R. R. of New Jersey and, at the bottom, the National Docks Railway cross the sheet from the upper left to the lower right and carry on to sheet 60, with a small power house standing between the Lehigh Valley and Central tracks. The large blocks between the lines are numbered 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2154. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet and 16 inch and 6 inch water mains are marked along Pacific Avenue and the vertical margin carries the words See Volume Nine. A compass rose with its north arrow sits at the top left of the sheet, with north towards the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and adjoins sheets 56, 60 and 64.
notes: Pacific, Carteret and Caven Point Avenues keep their names in OpenStreetMap; the Pacific Avenue junctions with Caven Point and Carteret Avenues lie on the cut edges of the sheet and were hand picked from the street centres.
Whiton Street does not reach Carteret Avenue today; the short street drawn here is not in OpenStreetMap.
The vertical margin text reads See Volume Nine.
50 ft. Pacific, Caven Point, Carteret strip with foundry and rail lines; 2 hand-picked points.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 continues the Pacific Avenue frontage east of sheet 59. Pacific Avenue, 80 feet wide, runs across the top of the sheet with Carteret Avenue, 60 feet wide, crossing it at the upper left; the block on the left of Carteret Avenue belongs to sheet 59. South of Pacific Avenue the sheet is mostly open ground within city blocks 2023 and 2022, bounded by Whiton, a 30 foot street running east from Carteret Avenue, and by Pine, a 50 foot street along the lower edge of the block. A pair of small frame dwellings and a narrow shed stand on the Pacific Avenue frontage towards the upper right, and a group of pink brick buildings stands against the right margin, where the plant continues on sheet 61. Lehigh Valley R. R. tracks cross the lower half of the sheet from the upper left to the lower right, with a branch curving away at the right, and below them lies the wide spread of Central R. R. of New Jersey yard tracks inside block 2154, with block 2021 between the two railroads. Street widths and 16 inch and 6 inch water mains are lettered along Pacific Avenue. A compass rose at the top right shows north towards the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and adjoins sheets 55, 59, 61 and 64.
notes: Pacific and Carteret Avenues keep their names in OpenStreetMap; their junction was hand picked on the sheet.
The drawn Whiton and Pine streets east of Carteret Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap at these positions; modern Whiton and Pine Streets lie further north-east.
50 ft. Pacific/Carteret, Whiton, Pine blocks and rail lines; anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 shows a district of foundries and machine works between Pacific Avenue on the left and the Lehigh Valley R. R. on the right, drawn with north towards the upper left. Pacific Avenue, 80 feet wide, runs up the left side with Forrest Street crossing it at the lower left; Whiton and Pine, two parallel streets, run up the sheet to the right of it, Pine marked as not opened, and a cross street between block 2031 and block 2032 links them. The largest building is the pink brick machine shop of the A. B. See Electric Elevator Co. in block 2023 and 2022, with a boiler and engine house and receiving and shipping department at its south end. Other works named on the sheet are the New York Metallic Bedstead Co. (foundry, machine shop and factory buildings) on Pacific Avenue, the Standard Motor Construction Co., makers of marine gasoline engines, between Whiton and Pine, and The Shead and Co. iron foundry, with its fitting shop, concrete foundation and cleaning building, to the right of Pine. The Newark and New York R. R. crosses the upper left diagonally and curved sidings serve the works; the Lehigh Valley R. R. runs along the right edge. Each works carries its watchman and fire-protection notes, and numbered blocks 2031, 2032 and 2033 are printed. A compass rose sits at the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and adjoins sheets 54, 55, 57, 58, 60 and 64.
notes: Pacific Avenue and Forrest Street keep their names in OpenStreetMap; their junction anchors the placement.
The drawn Whiton and Pine streets between the works are not in OpenStreetMap at these positions.
50 ft. Foundries between Pacific Av and Lehigh Valley RR; anchored on one point.

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 is a 100 feet to an inch sheet of the Central R. R. of New Jersey terminal at Communipaw in Jersey City, drawn with north towards the upper left. Garrabrant, a 60 foot street marked not opened south of Maple Street, runs down the left side of the sheet from Johnstone Avenue at the top to Communipaw Avenue at the bottom. Johnstone Avenue runs across the top to the right and then turns north-east to meet Jersey Avenue at the upper right; Wilson runs up from Communipaw Avenue at the lower right and a new Communipaw Avenue crosses on an iron bridge over the tracks. The yards fill the middle and right: the Lehigh Valley R. R., the National Docks Railway and the broad fan of Central R. R. of New Jersey yard tracks converge on the Central R. R. of New Jersey round house, drawn as a semicircle with its turntable, with a water tank, an office and the Communipaw station of the C. R. R. of N. J. near the bottom. On Garrabrant stand the lumber sheds and piles of H. Hermann Lumber Co., and the sawn lumber yard of a lumber and supply firm lies below Johnstone Avenue. Blocks 2048 and the surrounding numbers 46, 48, 52, 58, 62, 63, 66 and 69 are printed. Fire alarm boxes stand at the corners. A compass rose is at the upper left.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue and Garrabrant is Garabrant Street in OpenStreetMap.
Maple Street and Wilson do not survive at these positions.
Placed from the Garabrant and Johnston junction only; the OpenStreetMap Jersey Avenue junction lies about 90 feet from the drawn one.
100 ft. CRR Communipaw roundhouse yard; anchored on Garrabrant/Johnstone.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the open ground of the Mill Creek and the railroad yards between Pacific Avenue and Johnstone Avenue on the south-eastern edge of the volume. Pacific Avenue crosses the upper left corner, where the Morris Canal and its tow path pass under it and turn east along the top of the sheet. Below, the ends of Whiton, Pine, Monitor and Garrabrant Streets stop at the line of the National Docks Railway, which runs down the left side on a steel trestle beside a coal yard. The Lehigh Valley Terminal Railway fans out in a long curving yard of parallel sidings through the middle of the sheet, and Mill Creek winds through the marsh to the east, the area beyond being marked 'See Volume One'. In the lower part the Lehigh Valley Railroad cattle pens and a timber yard lie along the tracks, with a covered overhead pass, a gate tower and a locomotive house near Jersey Avenue, which crosses the lower right corner to meet Johnstone Avenue at the bottom. Block number 2145 is printed in the yard.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point (Jersey Avenue / Johnstone Avenue) with the scan scale and north set from the bearing of Johnston Avenue; the bend of Johnstone Avenue agrees with the modern road; Pacific Avenue in the far corner is about 10 m off; low confidence.
Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue, Garrabrant Street is Garabrant Street in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft. Mill Creek, Lehigh Valley yard and cattle pens, Pacific Av to Johnstone Av; anchored on hand-picked Jersey Av / Johnstone Av.

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the Central Railroad of New Jersey yards at Communipaw, east of Jersey Avenue and south of the Tidewater Basin. Jersey Avenue runs down the left edge and Johnstone Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet from Jersey Avenue towards the terminal. North of Johnstone Avenue lie the tracks of the Lehigh Valley Terminal Railway, with the property line between the Lehigh Valley and the Central Railroad marked, and along the top the Tidewater Basin with Pier L and the old Jersey City and Bergen boundary line, beyond which the sheet is marked 'See Volume One'. In the upper left corner the United Building Material Co. occupies cement storage sheds and cattle pens beside Jersey Avenue. On Johnstone Avenue stand the railroad's machine shop, officials' car shed, offices and a turntable with radiating stalls; coal pockets and the Lester Fellows cement storage stand among the tracks. The rest of the sheet, more than half of it, is filled with the parallel and fanning tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard, with block number 2145. Phillip Street appears at the lower left edge with two small buildings. Water pipes of 10 and 20 inches run along Johnstone Avenue, the latter owned by the Central Railroad.
notes: Johnstone Avenue is Johnston Avenue in OpenStreetMap; it still follows the drawn line east of Jersey Avenue into Liberty State Park.
Placed from one hand-picked point (Jersey Avenue / Johnstone Avenue) with the scan scale and north set by the bearing of Johnston Avenue; low confidence.
The whole yard is now Liberty State Park.
100 ft. CRR yards at Johnstone Av and Jersey Av, Tidewater Basin; anchored on hand-picked Jersey Av / Johnstone Av.

sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and continues the Central Railroad of New Jersey yards at Communipaw eastward from sheet 69. Along the top are the slips of the Tidewater Basin with Pier 1 and Pier 6, followed by the tracks of the Lehigh Valley Terminal Railway and the property line between the Lehigh Valley Railway and the Central Railroad of New Jersey. The old boundary line between Jersey City and Bergen crosses the upper part diagonally, and the area north of it is marked 'See Volume One'. Johnstone Avenue runs across the upper third of the sheet with water pipes along it; Burns Bros. coal pockets stand beside it at the right. Below, the sheet is filled with the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard (block 2145), with a small switch tower and a locomotive house. In the lower right the yard reaches the water: Pier No. 9 carries an incline trestle to coal pockets, and Piers No. 10 and No. 11, on piles, project into the bay, with slips between them outlined in blue.
notes: Placed only from three points carried across the shared edge from sheet 69 (no surviving street junction); rotation and scale as sheet 69; low confidence.
Johnstone Avenue (Johnston Avenue today) agrees with the modern road to a few metres in an overlay.
100 ft. CRR yards, Tidewater Basin, piers 9-11; placed from 3 points carried from sheet 69 across the shared edge.
